## `scripts/sim/city_sim.gd`

class_name `CitySim` · extends `Node`

Tile-based SimCity-style simulation: zoning + demand-driven growth, power/water/sewage networks with load shedding, service coverage, pollution/crime/land value/traffic maps, per-district budgets and taxes, city-wide ordinances, disasters, time speeds, save/load.

### Signals

- `tiles_changed(indices: PackedInt32Array)`
- `day_started(day: int)`
- `day_ended(day: int)`
- `territory_changed(mi: int)`
- `stats_updated()`
- `event_started(ev: Dictionary)`
- `event_ended(ev: Dictionary)`
- `city_log(message: String, category: String)`
- `waiting_changed(waiting: bool)`
- `tick_done(tick: int)`
- `incident_progress(ev: Dictionary)`
- `site_started(site: Dictionary)`
- `site_stage(site: Dictionary)`
- `site_finished(site: Dictionary)`
- `tick_progress(phase: String, fraction: float)`: Progress of a sliced tick; phase is a stable name ("recompute", "growth", "construction", "incidents", "residents", "commit", "day_end"); fraction 0..1 within the whole tick.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `N4 = [Vector2i(0, -1), Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(-1, 0)]`
- `UNITS_PER_PUMP = 32`: Sliced work is counted in units: one unit is a chunk of at most UNIT_WORK tile visits, one road search that misses the route cache, or one resident's turn. A pump starts no step once it has done UNITS_PER_PUMP - STEP_MAX_UNITS units, and a step (with its nested synchronous sections) stays within STEP_MAX_UNITS, so one pump never exceeds UNITS_PER_PUMP on any machine.
- `STEP_MAX_UNITS = 8`
- `UNIT_WORK = 2048`

### Properties

- `sliced: bool`: Time-sliced ticking for first person. false (default): _process runs step_tick() synchronously, exactly as today. true: a due tick runs as a resumable job, at most slice_budget_ms per frame. Switching finishes any job in flight first, so teardown's `sliced = false` never abandons a tick.
- `spread_gate: Callable`: Set by ResidentMinds: true while it spreads the day's plan batches over frames. begin_tick() waits for it, and _finish_job_now() drains it through spread_finish.
- `road_epoch: int`: Bumped whenever a tile turns into a road or stops being one (route caches key on it).
- `day_seconds: float`: Real seconds per game day at speed 1. Orbit and tests keep SimDefs.BASE_DAY_SECONDS (12); first person sets WS.FP_DAY_SECONDS (1200). Not saved: the view mode sets it at boot. Change it through set_day_seconds() while a day is running, so the time of day stays put.
- `people: Residents`: The AI residents (Residents node). When attached, human behaviour (mood, commuting, spending, moving, fixing what breaks) comes from their decisions instead of fixed formulas.
- `broken_roads: Dictionary`: Road tiles cut by a downed power line: tile -> incident id.
- `active`: Tiles the per-tick systems process: claimed land plus a small margin. Unclaimed wilds hold no roads or buildings, so skipping them keeps a 192x192 world as cheap as the founding city.
- `sites: Dictionary`: Open construction sites: tile -> site. "auto" stages construction whenever residents run the city; "staged" / "instant" force it either way.
- `load_remap: Dictionary`: Set by from_dict when the save used an older world layout: {w, h, x0, y0} of that layout, so other systems (residents) can move their saved tile indices across with remap_index.

### Functions

- `func new_city(seed_value: int) -> void`
- `func district_rect(d: int) -> Rect2i`: Bounding box of the tiles district d owns (it grows as the mayor annexes plots).
- `func plot_claimed(p: Vector2i) -> bool`: A plot is claimed once any of its tiles belongs to a district (annexation takes whole plots; the founding city's districts split its plots between them).
- `func is_surveyed(x: int, y: int) -> bool`: Whether tile x,y lies on surveyed land (claimed or within SURVEY_RANGE plots of it).
- `func surveyed_plots() -> Array`
- `func owned_rect() -> Rect2i`: Union of all districts: the developed part of the world.
- `func owner_name(i: int) -> String`
- `func annex_cost(mi: int) -> int`
- `func annexable_plots(mi: int) -> Array`: Plots that are entirely unclaimed and share an edge with land district mi already owns.
- `func set_speed(s: int) -> void`
- `func day_progress() -> float`
- `func tick_seconds() -> float`: Real seconds per growth tick at speed 1.
- `func set_day_seconds(s: float) -> void`: Changes the day length and rescales the time already accumulated toward the next tick, so day_progress() and tick_phase() are unchanged (a raw switch from a 1200 s to a 12 s day would leave up to a whole 300 s tick pending and run dozens of ticks at once).
- `func set_tick_phase(p: float) -> void`: Sets how far the current growth tick has run (0..1), e.g. when a save restores the time of day. A sliced tick in flight then commits without taking its time back out of the accumulator.
- `func skip_to_next_day() -> bool`: Runs the rest of today's growth ticks synchronously so the next day starts at dawn (FP "skip to morning"). Stops early if the day gate holds the boundary. Returns true when the new day has started. In sliced mode it first completes the job in flight.
- `func step_tick() -> void`
- `func start() -> void`: Emits day_started for the very first day (call once after wiring listeners).
- `func day_start_deferred() -> bool`: True while the sliced day job emits day_started: Residents then leaves its day-start work to begin_day() / pump_day(), which the job runs after the emission.
- `func work_based() -> bool`: True when residents decide behaviour; incidents then end only when someone fixes them.
- `func global_tick() -> int`
- `func begin_tick() -> bool`: Starts a sliced tick now if none is in flight and the day gate is open (waiting_for_ai false). Returns true if a job started. _process calls it when _time_accum reaches a tick; tests call it.
- `func pump(budget_ms: float) -> bool`: Advances the in-flight sliced job by up to budget_ms of work. It never starts a new tick (that is begin_tick's job). Returns true if a tick committed during this call. While ResidentMinds spreads a reaction the job raised, the job waits (the reaction comes first, as in the synchronous path).
- `func spread_allowed() -> bool`: True when listeners may spread work over frames (ResidentMinds' plan batches and reactions, a registered spread source): sliced, and not inside a forced synchronous tick (step_tick, load). The job waits for them.
- `func spread_pending() -> bool`: True while ResidentMinds or a registered spread source still has work waiting for a frame; the sliced job and begin_tick() wait meanwhile.
- `func add_spread_source(gate: Callable, finish: Callable) -> void`: Registers a listener that spreads work it would otherwise do inside a job emission (day_started, event_started) over later frames, e.g. CityBrain's mayors. While gate() returns true the sliced job waits (begin_tick() starts nothing, pump() does nothing), so the work lands at the same point as in the synchronous path, and _finish_job_now() calls finish() to run the rest at once. A day_started listener spreads only when day_start_deferred() is true (the emission comes from the sliced day job, which holds Residents' day work until the gate closes); other emissions only while spread_allowed() is true. Each deferred piece, and each piece finish() runs, goes through run_in_phase(). Registering the same gate again replaces its finish.
- `func remove_spread_source(gate: Callable) -> void`
- `func run_in_phase(f: Callable) -> void`: Runs f as part of the sliced job's current phase: work a spread source deferred from a job emission. Mutators inside f neither finish the job nor recompute on the spot; a recompute they owe runs as a sub-job right after f, before the job resumes. With no job in flight (or inside a step) it just calls f. f must not await: a live call that resumes later comes back through here.
- `func is_tick_running() -> bool`: True while a sliced tick is between start and commit.
- `func job_pending() -> bool`: True while any sliced job is in flight: a tick, the day boundary after its commit, or a recompute queued by a mutator.
- `func slice_stats() -> Dictionary`: Per-pump timings since the last reset: {"pumps", "ticks", "max_ms", "p95_ms", "over_budget", "max_units" (largest number of work units in one pump, nested sync sections counted), "sync_max_ms" (the longest forced synchronous finish, reported separately)}, plus "brain_ms" (longest day_started emission, the brain's listeners; excluded from max_ms), "view_ms" (longest tiles_changed emission, the view rebuild; excluded), "sync_finishes" (how many forced finishes), "units_limit", "max_step_units", "slowest_step_ms" / "slowest_phase" and "avg_ms".
- `func slice_profile() -> Dictionary`: Per step kind ("phase:stage"): [steps, max_ms, max_units, total_ms] since the last reset.
- `func reset_slice_stats() -> void`
- `func note_units(n: int) -> void`: Counts n extra work units in the current pump (a road search, a full-map scan inside a step).
- `func step_heavy() -> bool`: True inside a pumped step that already paid for a heavy item (a road search or a full scan): loops that take several items per unit stop there.
- `func job_yield_requested() -> bool`: True inside a job step that queued a nested task: resumable loops stop after the current item so the nested task runs before them.
- `func power_need(i: int) -> float`
- `func water_need(i: int) -> float`
- `func waste_need(i: int) -> float`
- `func sewage_need(i: int) -> float`
- `func commute(x: int, y: int) -> float`
- `func tile_pop(i: int) -> int`
- `func tile_jobs(i: int) -> int`
- `func staged() -> bool`: Staged construction is on whenever residents run the city, unless forced either way.
- `func add_site_work(i: int, amount: float, who: String) -> bool`: Adds construction work to the site on tile i. Returns true once the whole site is finished.
- `func crew_names(s: Dictionary, max_n: int) -> Array`: Builders on a site, residents first, then the contractor.
- `func finish_all_sites() -> void`: Finishes every open site at once (showcase and tests).
- `func tick_phase() -> float`: 0..1 progress through the current growth tick, so views can interpolate between ticks.
- `func zone_site_counts() -> Array`: Open developer (zone) sites per district.
- `func site_fraction(s: Dictionary) -> float`: 0..1 completion of a site across all its stages.
- `func site_stage_name(s: Dictionary) -> String`
- `func site_info(i: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func site_summary(d: int, max_n: int = 8) -> Array`: Short lines describing a district's open sites, for prompts and the HUD.
- `func total_funds() -> int`
- `func apply_action(mi: int, a: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`: Applies one AI (or player) action for the mayor at index mi. Returns {ok, reason, cost}.
- `func enact_ordinance(key: String) -> bool`
- `func repeal_ordinance(key: String) -> bool`
- `func gift_funds(mi: int, amount: int) -> void`
- `func trigger_disaster(type_name: String, x: int, y: int, source: String = "player", reason: String = "") -> Dicti`
- `func add_incident_work(ev_id: int, amount: float, who: String) -> bool`: Adds repair/response work to an incident and resolves it once enough work is done.
- `func find_event(ev_id: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func resolve_incident(ev: Dictionary, finisher: String) -> void`
- `func resident_left(home_i: int) -> void`: A resident moving away empties part of their building.
- `func clear_all_events() -> void`
- `func district_summary(d: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func tile_char(i: int) -> String`
- `func district_ascii(d: int) -> String`
- `func open_lots(d: int, max_n: int = 14) -> Array`: Empty land tiles in district d next to a road (best spots for zoning/buildings).
- `func city_summary() -> Dictionary`
- `func sample_citizens(n: int) -> Array`
- `func tile_report(x: int, y: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`: A save taken while a sliced job runs completes it first, so it equals the save after the equivalent synchronous tick.
- `func from_dict(data: Dictionary) -> bool`

## `scripts/sim/residents.gd`

class_name `Residents` · extends `Node`

The people of GridFall: up to 100 named residents, each standing in for an equal share of the population. Their GMI minds (ResidentMinds) choose how they commute, spend, feel, whether they stay, and whether they help when something breaks. This node turns those choices into the traffic, mood, money and repair work that CitySim reads.

### Signals

- `resident_arrived(r: Dictionary)`
- `resident_departed(r: Dictionary, reason: String)`
- `resident_moved(r: Dictionary)`
- `day_ready(day: int)`
- `resident_said(id: String, text: String, kind: String)`: A resident spoke out loud or wrote to their mayor. kind: "say" (daily plan line), "react" (incident reaction line), "letter" (message to the mayor). text is never empty.
- `trip_started(id: String, from_i: int, to_i: int, mode: String)`: A resident set off from tile from_i to tile to_i (sim arrival is instant; the view animates the trip). mode: car | bus | bike | walk.

### Constants

- `D = preload("res://scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd")`
- `MAX_RESIDENTS = 100`
- `PEOPLE_PER_RESIDENT = 10.0`: One named resident per this many people until the cap is reached.
- `WAGE_SCALE = 0.0175`: Personal dollars -> city tax base for the share of people a resident stands for.
- `SALES_SCALE = 0.06`
- `TRIP_SCALE = 0.35`
- `MODE_WEIGHT = {"car": 1.0, "bus": 0.25, "bike": 0.05, "walk": 0.0, "stay_home": 0.0}`
- `LIVING_COST = 30`
- `N4 = [Vector2i(0, -1), Vector2i(1, 0), Vector2i(0, 1), Vector2i(-1, 0)]`
- `RES_PER_UNIT = 4`: Residents handled per work unit of a sliced tick, and the route-search cache size (one 192x192 parent map per origin road tile).
- `BFS_CACHE_MAX = 160`
- `COMMUTES = ["car", "bus", "bike", "walk", "stay_home"]`
- `SPEND_WHERE = ["local", "downtown", "online", "none"]`
- `EVENINGS = ["home", "shopping", "park", "stadium", "visit_friend", "help_neighbors", "protest", "w...`
- `INTENTS = ["stay", "considering_leaving", "leaving"]`
- `COMPLAINTS = ["none", "power", "water", "sewage", "trash", "pollution", "crime", "traffic", "taxes",...`
- `ACTIONS = ["help", "report", "avoid", "evacuate", "ignore"]`
- `OCCUPATIONS = { "electrician": {"skills": ["power", "construction"], "wage": 210, "at": [D.ZONE_I, D....`: wage is personal dollars per working day; "at" lists the tile kinds that employ them.
- `FIRST_NAMES = ["Ava", "Ben", "Chen", "Dara", "Eli", "Fatima", "Gus", "Hana", "Ivan", "Jade", "Kofi", ...`
- `LAST_NAMES = ["Diaz", "Okafor", "Nguyen", "Kowalski", "Haddad", "Silva", "Brennan", "Tanaka", "Petro...`
- `TRAITS = ["anxious", "frugal", "sociable", "stubborn", "optimistic", "proud", "lazy", "caring", ...`
- `HOUSEHOLDS = ["lives alone", "lives with a partner", "single parent of one", "parent of two young ki...`

### Properties

- `share: float`: People each resident stands for right now.

### Functions

- `func setup(p_sim: CitySim) -> void`
- `func is_active() -> bool`
- `func key(r: Dictionary) -> String`
- `func find(id: String) -> Dictionary`
- `func district_money() -> Array`
- `func rebuild_maps() -> void`
- `func maps_step(st: Dictionary, lim: int) -> bool`: One step of a resumable rebuild_maps() that keeps its state in st (CitySim's recompute task, or a fresh dictionary): share, road signature, trips (one origin's road search per unit), mood map and sentiment, in that order. lim is this call's work budget in tile visits. True when done.
- `func district_mood(d: int) -> Dictionary`
- `func messages_for(d: int, max_n: int = 6) -> Array`
- `func begin_day(day: int) -> void`: Starts the day-start work (moves, new jobs, arrivals, maps, then day_ready) as a resumable job.
- `func pump_day(budget_ms: float) -> bool`: Advances the day-start job: one unit when budget_ms <= 0, else units until budget_ms is spent. Emits day_ready and returns true when the job is done.
- `func day_job_running() -> bool`: True while a sliced day-start job is in flight.
- `func begin_tick(t: int) -> void`: Starts tick t's resident work (the daily routine phase, then helpers on sites and incidents) as a resumable job.
- `func pump_tick(budget_ms: float) -> bool`: Advances the tick job: one unit when budget_ms <= 0, else units until budget_ms is spent. Stops early when the sim queued nested work (an incident resolved). True when the tick's work is done.
- `func abort_jobs() -> void`: Drops the sliced tick and day jobs (the sim replaced the city).
- `func rent_for(r: Dictionary) -> int`
- `func build_amount(r: Dictionary) -> float`: One resident is a fraction of a contractor crew (CREW_RATE per tick), but a few local builders working the morning and midday shifts roughly double a site's pace.
- `func help_amount(r: Dictionary, ev: Dictionary) -> float`
- `func apply_plan(r: Dictionary, d: Dictionary, source: String, model: String) -> void`
- `func respond(r: Dictionary, ev: Dictionary, d: Dictionary, source: String, model: String) -> String`
- `func remember(r: Dictionary, line: String) -> void`: Adds a line to the resident's memory as "Day N: line" (an exact repeat of the last line is skipped, at most 8 lines kept). For other slices, e.g. a face-to-face conversation that ends.
- `func nudge_mood(r: Dictionary, delta: float) -> void`: Shifts the resident's mood (0..10) by delta, clamped. Callers bound delta themselves.
- `func route_between(a: int, b: int) -> Array`
- `func card(r: Dictionary) -> Dictionary`
- `func to_dict() -> Dictionary`
- `func from_dict(d: Dictionary) -> void`

## `scripts/sim/sim_defs.gd`

class_name `SimDefs` · extends `RefCounted`

Static rules, costs, and catalogs for the GridFall city simulation.

### Constants

- `CORE = 32`: Founding city size; the world around it is six times wider in each direction.
- `W = 192`
- `H = 192`
- `X0 = -80`
- `Y0 = -80`
- `PLOT = 16`
- `NO_TILE = Vector2i(-99999, -99999)`: "No tile" marker: -1 is a real coordinate in the wider world.
- `ANNEX_BASE_COST = 1500`
- `ANNEX_STEP_COST = 400`
- `SURVEY_RANGE = 2`: Plots within this many plots of claimed land are surveyed: mapped and shown clearly. The frontier beyond stays in haze until the city grows towards it.
- `LEGACY_WORLD = {"w": 96, "h": 96, "x0": -32, "y0": -32}`: Layout of saves written before the world grew to 192x192.
- `GROWTH_TICKS_PER_DAY = 4`
- `BASE_DAY_SECONDS = 12.0`
- `START_FUNDS = 12000`
- `EMPTY = 0`
- `ROAD = 1`

- `ZONE_I = 4`

- `WATER = 1`
- `KIND_NAMES = { EMPTY: "empty", ROAD: "road", ZONE_R: "residential", ZONE_C: "commercial", ZONE_I: "i...`
- `BUILDINGS = { "coal_plant": {"kind": COAL, "cost": 3000, "upkeep": 45, "power": 140, "pollution": 1...`: Buildable service structures. power/water/sewage are capacities supplied; radius is coverage.
- `ROAD_COST = 10`
- `ZONE_COST = 5`

- `ROAD_TICKS = 4`: Contractor-only build times in growth ticks (4 ticks = 1 day). Resident crews shorten them.
- `BRIDGE_TICKS = 10`
- `ZONE_SITE_TICKS = {"zone_house": 8, "zone_new": 10, "zone_up": 14, "zone_tower": 24}`
- `HELPER_CAP = 0.6`: Resident helpers can add at most this share of a contractor shift to one site per tick, so a keen neighbourhood speeds a job up without building a stadium in a weekend.
- `MAX_ZONE_SITES = 10`: Private developers in one district only take on this many zone sites at a time.
- `SITE_STAGES = { "build": ["clearing", "excavation", "foundation", "frame", "finishing"], "light": ["c...`
- `STAGE_LABELS = { "clearing": "clearing the land", "excavation": "digging the foundations", "foundation...`
- `LIGHT_BUILDS = ["solar_farm", "wind_farm", "landfill"]`: Light structures skip the excavation stage.
- `R_POP = [0, 16, 48, 120]`
- `C_JOBS = [0, 10, 30, 72]`
- `I_JOBS = [0, 14, 40, 90]`
- `ORDINANCES = { "public_transit": {"label": "Public Transit Network", "cost": 60, "desc": "-30% traff...`
- `DISASTERS = { "fire": {"label": "Building Fire", "days": 2, "work": 60, "skills": ["fire", "rescue"...`: "days" is only used when no residents are simulated. With residents, an incident stays broken until people or paid crews put in "work" points; "skills" say who is actually useful, and "weather" incidents also fade by that much per tick on their own.
- `SKILL_LABELS = { "power": "electrical repair", "water": "water and pipes", "sewage": "sewage systems",...`
- `MAYORS = [ { "id": "argon", "name": "Argon-4", "display": "Ada Okafor", "model": "google/gemini-...`: Five autonomous AI mayors, each powered by a different GMI Cloud model.
- `SUPPORT_AGENTS = { "citizens": {"name": "Citizen Voices", "model": "MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3", "color": "#7F...`: Supporting GMI agents that give the rest of the city a mind.

### Functions

- `static func idx(x: int, y: int) -> int`: The founding city keeps coordinates 0..31 so recorded mayor actions and saves stay valid; the wider world runs from X0/Y0 (-80) to 111 and is opened up plot by plot through annexation.
- `static func in_bounds(x: int, y: int) -> bool`
- `static func tx(i: int) -> int`
- `static func ty(i: int) -> int`
- `static func in_core(x: int, y: int) -> bool`

- `static func plot_rect(p: Vector2i) -> Rect2i`
- `static func is_zone(kind: int) -> bool`
- `static func is_service(kind: int) -> bool`
- `static func build_ticks(key: String) -> int`: Contractor-only build time in growth ticks (4 per day) for a service building.
- `static func is_power_plant(kind: int) -> bool`
- `static func building_key_for_kind(kind: int) -> String`
- `static func mayor_index(mayor_id: String) -> int`
- `static func mayor_display(mi: int) -> String`: Human display name of mayor mi ("" when out of range).
- `static func debrand(text: String) -> String`: Replaces model branding in free text (LLM output, replay cache, old saves) with display names: model ids (D.MAYORS[*].model) and brand names (D.MAYORS[*].name, also with a trailing ".x" or "-Flash" style suffix) become the display name; a bare brand word (Argon|DeepSeek|Kimi|Qwen|Grok, case-sensitive, whole word) becomes "Mayor <Surname>".
- `static func district_of(x: int, y: int) -> int`: Founding district layout: center 10x10 block for Kimi; four corner quadrants for the rest. Land outside the founding city belongs to nobody (-1) until a mayor annexes it.
- `static func district_bounds(d: int) -> Rect2i`
